text.p: Unisource said on Wednesday Italian telecoms firms Stet and Telecom Italia would join its AT&T-Unisource telecoms venture in Europe.
Unisource is a telecoms joint venture grouping Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT. AT&T Unisource is its 60-40 pct joint venture with AT&T Corp of the U.S.
In a separate move announced in the same statement Unisource said Stet /Telecom Italia would form a 50/50 strategic partnership with AT&T in Latin America.
The Italian group's Latin American venture with AT&T will deliver a portfolio of global services via two newly formed pan-American operating entities.

One will serve multinational customers, large and medium business, and high-end consumers throughout the region. The other will offer telecoms transport services to the region's telecommunications providers.

"The alliance between Stet/Telecom Italia and AT&T is based on the complementary expertise and strong local presence of the two partners and their affiliates in Latin America," the statement, issued in the Netherlands, said.
Unisource said Stet/Telecom Italia planned to take a significant stake in AT&T-Unisource Communications Services (AUCS).

AUCS offers telecoms services to businesses in Europe and globally via its membership of the WorldPartners Association. WorldPartners groups 16 telecom service providers, distributing services in over 30 countries.

Stet/Telecom Italia plans to distribute AT&T-Unisource services in Italy, in return the Italian group will transfer into AT&T-Unisource the relevant business activities of data and telecoms unit Telemedia International (TMI).

The statement said Stet/Telecom Italia would have the option to take a shareholding of up to 30 percent of AUCS. Ultimately the shareholdings are expected to be 40 percent for Unisource and 30 percent each for AT&T and Stet/Italia.

"Our link with AT&T in Latin America will allow us to grow from strength, since we already have a major presence on that continent," Stet/Telecom Italia chief executive Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano said in the statement.
"The relationship with AT&T and Unisource in Europe will help us to provide an even more competitive range of services to our customers," he added.

AT&T chief operating officer John Walter said the U.S. company was delighted to have Stet/Telecom Italia as a strategic partner. "Our businesses are highly complementary in both Europe and Latin America and our vision of the future is the same," he said.
AT&T's Latin American ambitions were said by industry watchers to have taken a blow after former Unisource partner Telefonica of Spain announced an alliance with a rival British/U.S. grouping.
